name: One-pot pargiot with potatoes & green beans (סיר פרגיות, תפוחי אדמה ושעועית ירוקה)

source.author: Instagram (Hebrew caption) — episode 51 of a home-cooking series
source.notes: A one-pot weeknight stew: onions fried ~15 min until golden, 1 kg diced pargiot (boneless chicken thighs) seasoned with chicken-grill spice, paprika, salt and pepper, small-diced potatoes, a little fried tomato paste, halved green beans and 2 cups boiling water, simmered ~30 min to a thick sauce. Served with white rice (not counted). Analyzed as 6 servings; 'generous olive oil' taken as ~4 tbsp, potatoes as 4 medium (~700 g), a frozen green-bean package as ~400 g. Manual intake — reference only, not adopted. Estimate.

steps: Heat olive oil in a sauté pan and fry the onion ~15 min until nicely golden.
Add the pargiot, season with grill spice, paprika, salt and pepper, and cook until half-browned.
Add the potato cubes and mix well.
Clear a space, fry the tomato paste briefly, then mix it through.
Pour in 2 cups boiling water, cover and cook on medium ~30 min until the potatoes are soft and the liquid reduces to a thick sauce.

batch_totals.note: Whole pot (6 servings), rice excluded. A genuinely complete meal on its own — protein, potato carbs, green-bean fibre. The 'generous' olive oil (~4 tbsp ≈ 500 kcal) plus pargit's own fat make up most of the fat.

him.verdict: A balanced, comforting one-pot meal: ~36 g protein, ~31 g carbs and ~5.7 g fibre per serving (~8 g protein per 100 kcal), already a full meal without the rice. Fat (~21 g) is the soft spot — 'generous' olive oil on top of pargit, which is fattier than breast. Cut the oil to 2 tbsp and it's an 8; adding rice turns it into a big ~650 kcal plate.
suggested_mods: Use 2 tbsp olive oil instead of 'generous' (−~40 kcal per serving) — a covered pot doesn't need much
Trim visible fat from the pargiot
Skip the rice or keep it to a small scoop — potatoes already supply the carbs
Double the green beans for more fibre and volume

her_preconception.verdict: A solid everyday dish for her: chicken protein with iron and zinc (thigh meat has more than breast), green beans for some folate and vitamin C, potatoes for potassium — all fully cooked by the 30-minute simmer. No safety flags.
prenatal_highlights: green beans (some folate, vitamin C); fully cooked
suggested_mods: Add a leafy salad on the side for extra folate

cooking_guide: Don't rush the onions — 15 minutes to a deep gold is where most of the sauce's flavour comes from.
Cut the potatoes small (as the recipe insists) so they cook through in 30 minutes and thicken the sauce.
Let the pargiot brown a little before stirring; crowding and constant stirring makes them steam.
Fry the tomato paste in a cleared spot of the pan for ~30 seconds before mixing — it removes the raw taste.
Use BOILING water so the simmer doesn't stall; keep it covered on medium and stir once or twice so nothing catches.
If the sauce is too thin at the end, uncover for a few minutes to reduce.
